topic: The Impossible Chessboard: Information Theory in Action
target_audience: University students (CS/Math majors or curious minds)

sections.title: The Hook: The Prisoner's Dilemma
lecture_lines: A warden challenges two prisoners with 64 coins.
One coin hides a key under the board.
They must identify the coin to survive.
animations: Create two prisoner characters on screen in #FFFFFF.
Draw a decision matrix box in #FF00FF for options.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Parity Bit (Information Foundation)
lecture_lines: Parity is a simple error-detecting code.
It tracks if coin counts are even or odd.
Think of it as a binary checksum balance.
animations: Create a bit stream sequence in #FFFF00.

sections.title: Mapping the Board to the Information Space
lecture_lines: We assign a unique binary index to each square.
Alice treats the board as a 64-bit string.
She calculates the parity of all heads-up coins.
Flipping one coin changes the total parity.
This forces the board to reveal the secret.
animations: Represent board state as an information vector in #FFFFFF.
Map board positions to bits in #00FFFF.
Color the board center in #FF00FF as key.

sections.title: The Solution: Communication through State Change
lecture_lines: Alice uses the board as a communication channel.
Changing parity points exactly to the hidden key.
Bob reads the board to recover the coordinate.
They survive with absolute, mathematical certainty.
The strategy transforms a guess into pure logic.
animations: Show two prisoners altering their shared board state.
Visualizing the state change as signal transmission in #FFFF00.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Power of Information Theory
lecture_lines: Logic transforms uncertainty into a solved puzzle.
This principle powers modern error correction protocols.
Information theory bridges abstract math and reality.
animations: Summarize prisoner strategy using bits in #FFFFFF.
